summary: Well-executed, fully preregistered paired experiment that is internally reproducible and artifact-rich, but the manuscript is overly provenance-heavy and lacks some concise, literature-grounded exposition and explicit operational definitions needed for reader comprehension and nearest-work positioning. The confirmatory result is degenerate (ceiling): identical shared-generation outputs produced 100% success in both baseline and guarded conditions, so the guarded validator/repair subsystem was never exercised. The run and analysis appear technically consistent and preregistration-compliant, but the paper requires modest manuscript revisions (clarifications and reframing) before finalisation.
critical_issues: Manuscript reads partially as an artifact inventory/provenance ledger rather than concise, literature-grounded scholarly prose; key narrative sections (Related Work, Positioning, and Discussion) should emphasize prior findings, mechanistic interpretation, and implications rather than long provenance dumps.

Operational definition of the primary outcome ("semantic failure" / pass–fail labeling) and the exact scoring rule mapping (e.g., what "full_intent_constraint_validation" entails) is not stated formally in one compact place in the manuscript; readers cannot verify how validator verdicts translate to the binary labels used in the McNemar test without hunting through archived JSON artifacts.

Nearest-work comparison is asserted qualitatively but lacks a compact, explicit comparison matrix tying this study to the closest prior experimental designs (which features are shared/different: shared-generation vs independent generation; emulator vs static syntactic checks; repair budget; task corpus provenance). The paper claims a methodological contribution but does not present the required nearest-work table in the main text.

The manuscript does not sufficiently justify the shared-generation design choice in the intro as a primary experimental design trade-off (it explains it later), nor does it plainly state that the shared-generation choice made the confirmatory test incapable of detecting repair utility when generator outputs are valid (this is discussed but should be more tightly linked to the interpretation of the hypothesis test).
required_revisions: Rewrite and reduce provenance-heavy passages in the main text: move long manifest lists, artifact path enumerations, and large provenance tables to a compact paragraph and explicitly reference the archived artifacts (file list + hashes) as supplementary material; replace those sections with concise, literature-grounded exposition emphasizing scientific interpretation and implications. (Resolvable from supplied artifacts/manuscript draft.)

Add a compact formal definition of the binary outcome used in the confirmatory test: state the scoring rule(s) used to produce pass/fail (name, version), show the exact decision logic (e.g., validator.violation_count>0 => fail; normalized_response==normalized_reference => pass; tie-break rules), and include one short concrete example illustrating a pass and a fail drawn from archived scoring artifacts. (Resolvable from supplied execution/scoring artifacts and validator traces.)

Include a concise nearest-work comparison matrix (1/2 page or compressed table) in the Related Work or Methods section that enumerates the closest prior experiments and explicitly marks where this study differs (shared-generation paired design, executable emulator validator, repair budget ≤1, synthetic deterministic task corpus, single hosted model). Cite the primary sources used to make each comparison. (Resolvable from the archived verified bibliography and evidence records.)

Tighten the framing of the shared-generation design in the Introduction and the Interpretation in Discussion: explicitly state as a preregistered design choice that a shared initial candidate isolates validator marginal effects but reduces probability of observing repair activity when the generator is well-calibrated; link this design choice to the observed ceiling outcome and to the limitations of the McNemar test under zero discordant pairs. (Resolvable by editing manuscript text.)
optional_revisions: Add a short illustrative hypothetical or simulation (textual description only — not new experiments) showing how independent per-condition generation or targeted selection of 'very_hard' tasks would increase discordant-pair incidence and make the primary test informative; refer to the task_manifest difficulty fields to indicate specific thresholds to use in future runs. (Can be done from archived task manifest.)

Condense and integrate the Disclosure Statement so it remains complete but less disruptive to narrative flow (for example, use a short inline summary and point to the full archived disclosure artifact). Ensure the Disclosure remains within pages 1–5. (Resolvable by editing manuscript text and re-checking page count.)

Expand a brief paragraph on how the validator encodes workflow policies (must_be_down_for_fields, final_group_constraints, make-before-break) into executable checks and limitations of that encoding (vendor heterogeneity, partial observability), using representative validator_trace snippets already archived as examples. (Resolvable from validator traces in execution artifacts.)
